newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Brewers drop on bullish Nigerian bourse.
newsitem.headline: Brewers drop on bullish Nigerian bourse.

text.p: Nigerian equities continued to ride high in active Wednesday trading but shares of the leading brewers dropped as jittery investors resumed selling.
The all-share index closed at 7247.02 from 7227.45 on Tuesday.
Dealers said a new wave of selling gripped the biggest brewers, Nigerian Breweries and Guinness.
"Investors who wanted to offload million of units depressed their prices because of uncertainty over prospects in the sector," one trader said.
Nigerian Breweries fell 40 kobo to 16.00 naira. Guinness closed five kobo down at 8.00 naira.
Bank shares ended strongly. First Bank gained 20 kobo to end at 9.00. Union Bank was 10 kobo up at 7.92 naira and UBA rose to 7.45 naira, up five kobo.
Guaranty Trust Bank which announced a lower 9-month profit on Tuesday finished 10 kobo lower at 10.20 naira.
Sustained demand for food companies saw Nigerian Bottling Company rise 50 kobo to 35.50 naira and Cadbury by 20 kobo to 23.80 naira.
Oil shares finished higher despite the lingering fuel scarcity. Total was up 60 kobo at 63.80 naira while National Oil added 35 kobo to 52.50 naira.
Textile firms Abatex and Afprint dropped one kobo each to end at 3.61 naira and 2.59 naira, respectively.
Conglomerate PZ, whose merger with a susbidiary was effectively concluded on Wednesday, lost one kobo at 28.55 naira.
"Many investors are willing to sell some of their holding following a recent bonus issue but the market will mop up the excess in no time," said one dealer.
